INTRODUCTION
15
The People of Guam's (the "People") Motion to Dismiss Without Prejudice first came
16
17 before the Honorable Maria T. Cenzon on July 29, 2025, during the Pre-Trial Conference of this
18
case. Present at that hearing for the People was Assistant Attorney General John David Griffin.
19
Also present were Defendant Cameron Jose Guerrero ("Defendant") and counsel Thomas Fisher.
20
At the hearing, the Court addressed the People's Motion to Dismiss Without Prejudice ("Motion
21
22 to Dismiss"), which was filed the same day. The Court granted the Motion to Dismiss, but
23
reserved jurisdiction in order to resolve the question of prejudice. Pre-Trial Conference Hr'g
24
Mins. 7/29/2025 at 1:30:21 PM (July 29, 2025). The Court issued a briefing schedule on
25
September 19, 2025, and then again on January 9, 2026, after the Defendant failed to submit a
26
response to the People's Motion. See, Briefing Scheduling Order (Sep. 19, 2025); Am. Briefing
27
28 Scheduling Order (Jan. 8, 2026). After Defendant failed to submit its written counter-motion to

dismiss with prejudice on September 25, 2025, the Court extended the deadline to January 23,

2026. Despite the extension, Defendant failed to submit a response to the People's Motion or a

counter-motion. The Court then set the hearing on the motion for March 30, 2026, and notice was
4
served upon the parties Am. Notice ofH r 'g (Mar. 17, 2026).
5
During the March 30, 2026, hearing, Assistant Attorney General Martin Reming appeared
6
7 in person for the People. Defendant appeared by Zoom, but defense counsel Mr. Fisher did not
8
appear. Mins. OfM ot. Hrg. ofJ/30/2026 at 9:14:53 AM (Mar. 30, 2026). Following the hearing,

the Court took the matter under advisement pursuant to CVR 7 .1 ( e )( 6)(A) of the LOCAL RULES

OF THE SUPERIOR COURT OF GUAM.
II
12 After reviewing the pleadings on file, the prev10us arguments of counsel and the
13 applicable statutory and case law, the Court now issues the following Decision and Order
14
GRANTING the People's Motion to Dismiss Without Prejudice.
15
PROCEDURAL AND FACTUAL BACKGROUND
16
The Defendant was charged with Attempted Kidnapping (As a Second Degree Felony),
17
18 with notice of Commission of a Felony While on Felony Release; Attempted Second Degree
19
Robbery (As a Second Degree Felony), with notice of Commission of a Felony While on Felony
20
Release; Attempted Thef by Threatening (As a Misdemeanor); Reckless Conduct (As a
21
Misdemeanor); and Assault (As a Misdemeanor). Indictment (May 20, 2025). He was confined
22
following the Magistrate's Hearing on May 13, 2025 and held on $5,000 bond. Commitment
23
24 Order (May 13, 2025). The Defendant asserted his statutory right to a speedy trial on June 16,
25
2025. Def 's Assertion or Waiver ofS tat. Speedy Trial Rights & Request for Jury of1 2 in a Felony
26
Case (June 16, 2025). Trial was scheduled to begin on July 30, 2025. Criminal Trial Scheduling
27
Order (July 1, 2025).

The People filed a written Motion to Dismiss on July 29, 2026. The Motion requeste
2
dismissal without prejudice "in light ofrecent statements made from the alleged victim," indicatin
3
that he did "not want to testify in this matter" and did "not wish to pursue the charges." Mot.
4
Dismiss at 1 (July 29, 2025). At the continued Pre-Trial Conference the same day, the Peopl
5
stated that dismissal was necessary due to "witness availability problems." Pre-Trial Conferenc
6
7 Hr'g Mins. of 7/29/2025 at 1:27:51 PM to 1:29:57 PM. The People denied having a writte
8
statement from the victim expressing a desire not to testify, explaining that the victim did no
9
attend a scheduled interview with prosecution staff and investigators. Id at I :33:00 PM to 1: 33:2
PM. The Defendant argued that dismissal was not "for the proper purpose" and expressed conce
11
12 about his speedy trial rights. Id. at 1: 28:29 PM, 1: 30:43 PM. The Court granted the Motion t
13 dismiss and reserved the issue of whether dismissal should be with or without prejudice. Id. a
14
I :30:21 PM to I :30:29 PM.
15
The Court held a hearing on the question of whether to dismiss the case with or withou
16
prejudice on March 30, 2026, but defense counsel did not appear. Mot. Hr 'g Mins. of3 /30/2026 a
17
18 9:14:53 AM. The Defendant appeared via Zoom and stated that he had since been charged i
19
another case and convicted. Id. at 9:16:00 AM. The People and the Adult Probation Offic
20
informed the Court that the Defendant was awaiting sentencing for CF0865-25. Id at 9: 16:00 A

to 9:16:57 AM.
22
DISCUSSION
23
24 Guam law sets forth the procedure by which a prosecutor may seek dismissal of an
25
indictment:
26
The prosecuting attorney may with leave of court file a dismissal of an
27 indictment, information or complaint and the prosecution shall thereupon
terminate. Such a dismissal may not be filed during the trial without the consent of
28
the defendant. The prosecuting attorney shall file a statement of his reasons for
People v. Guerrero, Criminal Case No. CF0328-25
Decision and Order Re. People's Motion to Dismiss Without Prejudice
Page 3 of8

seeking dismissal when he applies for leave to file a dismissal and where leave is
granted the court's order shall set forth the reasons for granting such leave.
2
8 G.C.A. § 80.70(a). Section 80.70(a) does not distinguish between dismissal wit
3
4 prejudice and dismissal without prejudice. In considering a prosecutor's motion to dismiss unde
5
§ 80.70(a), the Guam Supreme Court has explained that "the prosecutor is recognized as having
6
presumption of good faith in bringing the motion ... and the motion should generally be grante
7
,r,r
as a matter of course." People v. Gutierrez, 2005 Guam 19 51-52. The presumption is no
8
,r
absolute and may be rebutted by a showing that the prosecution lacked good faith. Id. 53. But
9
10 trial court's review remains narrow: the court assesses whether the motion is contrary to th
11
manifest public interest because it is not based on the prosecutor's good faith discharge of he
12
,r
duties. Id. 57. Even when bad faith is shown,§ 80.70(a) generally authorizes the trial court onl
13
to grant or deny the prosecutor's motion; it does not authorize a trial court to sua sponte dismis
14
,r,r
15 an indictment with prejudice. Id. 69, 74-75.
16
When deciding whether dismissal should be with or without prejudice, trial courts conside
17
three factors: "(I) the seriousness of the offense; (2) the facts and circumstances of the case whic
18
led to the dismissal; and (3) the impact of a reprosecution on the administration of justice." Gua
19
,r
v. Aromin, 2014 Guam 3 21. The second factor includes, but is not limited to, "the facts an
20
21 circumstances surrounding the length of delay, government conduct, and actual prejudice suffere
22
by the defendant." Id. The Court applies those principles below.
23
A. The People's Motion satisfies 8 GCA § 80.70(a) and was brought in good faith.
24
The People complied with § 80.70(a)'s procedural requirements. The Motion was filed
25
before trial and contained a statement of reasons: the People represented that the alleged victim
26
27 recently indicated that he did not want to testify and did not wish to pursue the charges. Mot. to
28
Dismiss at 1. The People's explanation at the hearing record is consistent with that stated reason.
People v. Guerrero, Criminal Case No. CF0328~25
Decision and Order Re. People's Motion to Dismiss Without Prejudice
Page4 of8

The People identified "witness availability problems," explained that the alleged victim had
2
expressed reluctance to come forward, and further stated that the alleged victim did not appear at
3
a scheduled interview with prosecution staff. Pre-Trial Conf Hr 'g Mins. o/7/29/2025 at I :27:51
4
PM, 1:29:26 PM to 1:29:57 PM, 1:33:00 PM to 1:33:25 PM. The fact that the People did not
5
produce a statement from the victim requesting the case be dismissed or a statement from an
6
7 Office of the Attorney General Investigator describing the victim's reluctance is not sufficient to
8
establish bad faith. The People are entitled to a presumption of good faith, and the reason
9
provided-witness unavailability-is a vail reason to bring a motion to dismiss. Gutierrez, 2005
10
Guam 19 ml 51-52.
II
12 The Defendant questioned whether dismissal was being sought for an improper purpos
13
and expressed concern that dismissal might be used to stop the speedy trial clock. Pre-Tria
14
Conference Hr 'g Mins. of 7/29/2025 at 1:28:29 PM, 1:30:43 PM. But the Defendant filed n
15
written response after the Court issued a briefing schedule, and defense counsel failed to appear a
16
the March 30, 2026, hearing to argue the issue of prejudice. The Defendant has according!
17
18 presented no evidence that the People sought dismissal to harass him, evade his speedy trial rights
19 ,r,r
gain a tactical advantage, or otherwise act in bad faith. See Gutierrez, 2005 Guam 19 53-57
20
He has therefore failed to rebut the People's presumption of good faith.
21
B. The Aromin factors favor dismissal without prejudice.
22
1. The charged offenses are serious.
23
24 The first factor under Aromin weighs in favor of dismissal without prejudice. The Gu
25
Supreme Court has recognized that "the more serious the offense, the more weight should be give
26
,r
to dismissal without prejudice." Aromin, 2014 Guam 3 23 (citing United States v. Clymer, 25
27
F.3d 824,831 (9th Cir. 1994)). Here, the Indictment charges the Defendant with two second-degre
28
felony offenses and three misdemeanor offenses arising from alleged conduct directed at the sam
People v. Guerrero, Criminal Case No. CF0328~25
Decision and Order Re. People's Motion to Dismiss Without Prejudice
Page 5 of8

victim. Indict at 1-2. The attempted kidnapping charge is particularly serious because it require
2
not only unlawful confinement of another, but also the special intent to inflict bodily harm on o
3
terrorize that person. The charge of Attempted Second Degree Robbery is similarly seriou
4
because it also requires an element of violence; specifically, the threat of immediate serious bodil
5
injury. Indict. at 2; 9 G.C.A. § 40.20(a)(2). Furthermore, both felony offenses were charged wit
6
7 sentencing enhancements under 9 G.C.A. § 80.37.1 because the Defendant was already facing tria
8
on other felony charges. The misdemeanor offenses also allege acts of violence and threats. Indict.
9
at 3. While the offenses are classified as misdemeanors, they are still serious because of the violen
10
nature of the underlying conduct. For these reasons, the Court finds that the first Aromin facto
11
12 weighs in favor of dismissal without prejudice.
13
2. The facts and circumstances do not support dismissal with prejudice.
14
The second Aromin factor also favors dismissal without prejudice. This factor consider
15
the facts and circumstances surrounding the length of delay, government conduct, and actu
16
prejudice to the defendant. Aromin, 2014 Guam 3 ,i 21. In Aromin, the Guam Supreme Cou
17
18 affirmed the trial court's refusal to dismiss with prejudice where the defendant presented n
19 support showing actual prejudice, such as unavailable witnesses or missing or deteriorate
20
evidence, and was not "languishing in jail" awaiting initiation of the case. Id. ,i 24.
21
Here, the facts leading to dismissal are straightforward. The People sought dismissal o
22
July 29, 2025, after representing that the alleged victim did not want to testify or pursue charge
23
24 and after explaining at the hearing that the issue was witness availability. Mot. Dismiss at 1; Pre
25
Trial Coriference Hr 'g Mins. of 7/29/2025 at 1 :27:51 PM to 1 :29:57 PM. The Court grante
26
dismissal that day and stated the Defendant would be released on this matter. Pre-Trial Conj Hr '
27
Mins. o/7129/2025 at 1 :30:21 PM, 1 :35:36 PM. Although the Defendant had asserted his statuto
28
speedy trial right on June 16, 2025, he has not shown that the People moved to dismiss to evad
People v. Guerrero, Criminal Case No. CF0328-25
Decision and Order Re. People's Motion to Dismiss Without Prejudice
Page 6 of8

that right or that any delay caused actual prejudice to his defense. The record also reflects that, b
2
the March 30, 2026, hearing, the Defendant's custodial status was attributable to a separate cas
3
in which he had proceeded to trial, was convicted by a jury, and was awaiting sentencing. Mot.
4
Hr'g Mins. of 3/30/2026 at 9:16:00 AM to 9:16:57 AM.
5
6 Defendant's concern that dismissal might affect a future speedy trial calculation does not
7 standing alone, warrant dismissal with prejudice. If the People refile, Defendant may raise an
8
available speedy trial, statutory, or constitutional defenses in that proceeding. The question here i
9
whether this dismissal should bar reprosecution altogether. Because the record does not sho
actual prejudice to the Defendant or bad faith by the People, the second Aromin factor weighs i
l l
12 favor of dismissal without prejudice.
13
3. Reprosecution would not adversely affect the administration of justice.
14
The third Aromin factor-the impact of reprosecution on the administration of justice
15
also favors dismissal without prejudice. Dismissal with prejudice is a severe sanction. By contrast
16
dismissal without prejudice is not "a toothless sanction," because it requires the People to obtai
17
18 a new indictment if they decide to reprosecute, and may expose a future prosecution to statute-of
19 limitations or other procedural defenses. Aromin, 2014 Guam 3 ,i 25 (quoting Taylor v. Unite
20
States, 487 U.S. 326, 342 (I 988)).
21
The administration of justice is not served by dismissing serious charges with prejudic
22
where the dismissal was based on witness availability and where the defendant has not shown ba
23
24 faith or actual prejudice. The alleged conduct includes attempted unlawful confinement, allege
25
threats creating fear of inunediate serious bodily injury, and other violent acts. Indict. The publi
26
interest in allowing the People to reassess and, if appropriate, reprosecute serious allegation
27
weighs against an order permanently barring prosecution. At the same time, dismissal withou
28
People v. Guerrero, Criminal Case No. CF0328-25
Decision and Order Re. People's Motion to Dismiss Without Prejudice
Page 7 of8

prejudice preserves the Defendant's ability to challenge any future prosecution based on speed
2
trial, limitations, prejudice, or other grounds.
3
Moreover, the statute of limitations for a second-degree felony is three years after it
4
commission. 8 GCA § 10.20( c ). The allegations set forth in the Indictment aver that the inciden
5
occurred on April 22, 2025; therefore, the People must bring charges against the Defendant base
6
7 upon the allegations set forth in the Indictment by April 21, 2028. Dismissal with prejudice at thi
8
time would permanently bar prosecution for these offenses in the event that the named victi
9
becomes available to testify at the trial.
lO
After weighing the Aromin factors, the Court finds that the seriousness of the charge
11
12 offenses, the circumstances of the victim's unavailability leading to dismissal, the absence o
13 demonstrated bad faith or actual prejudice, and the limited adverse impact of any potentia
14
reprosecution all support dismissal without prejudice.
15
CONCLUSION
16
For the reasons set forth above, the People's Motion to Dismiss Without Prejudice is
17
18 GRANTED.
19 SO ORDERED this 29th day of July, 2026.
